story.see: No flood shows on this stretch of the Indus in 2026: the river channel stays the same. The change is farming. West of the river, fields darken in late July and August, then become very bright in September and October. A dark sand desert east of the river stays dark all season and is correctly not called water. The thin Indus channel is not picked up by our water layer at this resolution.
story.physics: Sindh is mostly arid; farming depends on the Indus and its canals. In the monsoon season many fields west of the river are flooded to grow rice. Once the paddies are planted the crop grows tall and dense through autumn until harvest.
story.lband: A newly flooded paddy mirrors the radar and turns dark in HH. As rice grows, the signal bounces between water and stems and back to the satellite, so the same fields become very bright. HV rises too as leaves fill in. The dark-then-bright pattern is a crop calendar written in radar.
story.people: Sindh had 55.7 million people in the 2023 census. Rice and other irrigated crops along the Indus feed the province and its cities. Seeing when fields are flooded and how the crop develops helps track water use and harvest timing across a whole province at once.

headlineNote: Co-polarised (HH) radar echo about 0.26 higher (0–1 brightness) inside a patch of changed echo of about 2,146 km² in the later passes
caution: Our water map holds no open water here, while NASA's OPERA water product maps 20–200 km². Read this place for the land change, not for water.

Radar echo outside the changed patch
steps: 1. Radar image before, 17 Jun–11 Jul (median of 3 passes, HH channel).
2. Radar image after, 21 Sep–15 Oct (median of 3 passes).
3. The difference: the echo rose by about 0.26 (0–1 brightness scale) inside a patch of about 2,146 km² of changed echo, summed over every changed patch in the frame.
4. A check: between 17 Jun–11 Jul, within the before group, the same pixels change by +0.01 on average, and 9 % of them cross the threshold, so the control is not clean.
5. It stays: the patch is still there on every later pass.

stats.area_label: area of changed radar echo, not a measurement of land cover, crop or forest loss
stats.unit_note: brightness units are the preview's 0-1 display scale; dB-like = 30 x brightness assumes a ~30 dB stretch (unverified)
stats.method_note: Preview brightness (uncalibrated, ~180 m), 3x3 boxcar + per-date gain normalisation; AFTER minus BEFORE (medians), 9x9 boxcar; threshold = median + 3.09 robust sigma of the same-signed change in a control built from two halves of a quiet interval (a Gaussian 99.9 % level that heavy tails do not inflate); connected patches of at least 5 km² kept, the one nearest the reference position (else the largest) reported. The area is the area of changed radar echo, not a measurement of land cover, crop or forest loss.
